consequence: The Groovy script `GLOVIA_Conditioncheck_Salesorder_Create.groovy` and header modifier `CallActivity_86` are present in BPMN definitions but disconnected from incoming/outgoing sequence flows. Any order code validation logic inside CallActivity_77 is silently bypassed at runtime.
mitigation: Unit tests TC_GLOVIA_001 and TC_GLOVIA_003 verify routing directly against the configured gateway conditions. Reconnecting CallActivity_77 before ExclusiveGateway_80 must be followed by tests validating OrderCodeValid header setting.

risk: Default Routing Escalation in One-Way CXF Adapter
consequence: When an incoming message does not match either SalesOrder or ReturnSalesOrder condition, EndEvent_11 raises an escalation error `RoutingConditionNotMet`. For asynchronous/one-way SOAP CXF endpoints, uncaught escalations may leave messages stuck in MPL without automated retry.
mitigation: TC_GLOVIA_003 validates that the escalation is explicitly raised with `RoutingConditionNotMet` and generates the expected SOAP Fault payload to alert monitoring systems.

risk: Large Message Payload Exceeding In-Memory Property Storage
consequence: CallActivity_4 reads the entire inbound message body into property `InputPayload` using `${in.body}`. For payloads approaching the 40MB maximumBodySize limit, this duplicates memory usage on the JVM worker node and risks OutOfMemoryError.
mitigation: TC_GLOVIA_005 verifies boundary handling and recommends streaming or selective persistence rather than in-memory property duplication.

risk: Unqualified SOAP Fault Element Lookup Failure
consequence: External consumer systems inspecting SOAP 1.1 Fault responses may fail parsing if namespaces are incorrectly applied to child elements (`faultcode`, `faultstring`).
mitigation: All unit assertions in `test_flow.py` strictly adhere to SOAP 1.1 specification standards where `Fault` has envelope qualification while `faultstring` and `detail` are unqualified.
